hero.title: Find out how much you'll get when you retire
hero.subtitle: Estimate your IESS pension in minutes and see how many more contributions, and what salary, you need to reach the pension you want.

step1.title: Enter your details
step1.body: Your number of monthly contributions, the average of your 5 best salary years, and your age.

step2.title: See your pension
step2.body: We show your estimated monthly pension, the extra yearly payments, and whether you already qualify.

step3.title: Set your goal
step3.body: Type the pension you want and we tell you how many more contributions, and what salary, you need to reach it.

rules.title: The rules, explained
rules.intro: The IESS calculates your pension from three things: how many years you contributed, the average of your 5 best salary years, and a coefficient. The pension also never goes below a minimum or above a maximum, both tied to the Unified Basic Salary (SBU).
rules.formula: Monthly pension = average of the 5 best years × coefficient (within the minimum and maximum caps).
rules.sbuNote: SBU {year} = {sbu}. The option that matches your current age applies.

q1.question: What is the SBU and why does it matter?
q1.answer: The Unified Basic Salary (SBU) is the minimum wage the Government sets every year. The IESS uses it to set the minimum and maximum pension, and for the fourteenth payment you receive as a retiree.

q2.question: How is my pension calculated?
q2.answer: The average of your 5 best salary years is multiplied by a coefficient that depends on your years of contributions. If the result is below the minimum or above the maximum for your range, it is adjusted to that cap.

q3.question: What is the average of the 5 best years?
q3.answer: It is the monthly average of the 60 months in which you earned the most. You can check it in your contribution history on the IESS website. If you don't know it, use an estimate.

q4.question: How many contributions do I need to retire?
q4.answer: It depends on your age: 480 contributions at any age, 360 if you are 60 or older, 180 if you are 65 or older, and 120 if you are 70 or older.

q5.question: Do I get extra payments each year?
q5.answer: Yes. You receive the thirteenth payment (one extra monthly pension) and the fourteenth payment (one extra SBU). That is why the yearly total is more than 12 pensions.

q6.question: Is this calculation official?
q6.answer: No. It is an informational estimate based on the published tables. To know your exact pension, check directly with the IESS.

elig.missing70: You don't qualify yet: you need {missing} more contributions for the age-70 requirement (120).
elig.missing65: You don't qualify yet: you need {missing} more contributions for the age-65 requirement (180).
elig.missing60: You don't qualify yet: you need {missing} more contributions for the age-60 requirement (360).
elig.under60: You don't qualify yet: under 60 you need 480 contributions.

desired.title: Desired pension
desired.needData: Enter an average of the 5 best years greater than 0 to run the simulation.
desired.reached: With monthly contributions on {salary} (IESS contribution: {iess}), you will reach your desired pension of {desired} in {months} more months, for a total of {total} contributions ({years} years).
desired.notReached: You don't reach the desired pension within 50 years of contributions with an adjusted salary of {salary}. Increase the adjusted salary.
desired.recommendation: Recommendation: the goal is to get the best value as soon as possible. It's better to contribute only up to {total} contributions ({years} years, or {extra} more contributions). At that point your pension hits the maximum cap of {cap}, and further contributions won't raise it until the next range. The maximum cap rises by range: {ranges}
desired.note: Adjusted monthly average: (average × 59 + salary) ÷ 60. Coefficient by full year of contributions (reference table). Pension to receive = adjusted average × coefficient (with SBU min/max caps when they apply).
desired.belowMin: The desired pension is below the minimum ({min}). You would receive at least {min}.
